description: Canonical, machine-readable readiness vocabulary for the Aether platform. This is the single source of truth for every readiness/capability token used by the certification plane (Python) and the presentation plane (TypeScript). It exists to end a real split-brain: Backend Architecture/aether-backend/shared/certification/readiness.py and frontend/shared/src/status/capability-state.ts previously defined overlapping-but-disagreeing vocabularies. Neither file is generated — both stay hand-written for ergonomics — but scripts/validate_readiness_vocabulary.py fails CI whenever the Python enum, the TypeScript union, this file, or packages/shared/contracts/evidence-manifest.schema.json disagree on membership, rank ordering, precedence ordering, or the production_ready-is-never-inferred rule.

rules.singleSource: No component may define a readiness token that is absent from this file, and no token here may lack a binding to at least one consumer (Python enum member or TypeScript union literal). A token with neither is dead vocabulary and must be deleted.
rules.rankScale: Certification ranks are spaced by 10 so future intermediate states can be inserted without renumbering. Only relative order is contractual; no consumer may depend on the absolute integers.
rules.offRampBelowProgression: Every certification token with progression=false must rank strictly below every token with progression=true, so that a `readiness_rank(x) >= readiness_rank(CREDENTIAL_WAITING)` gate can never admit an off-ramp state.
rules.inferableIsExhaustive: The set of tokens with inferable=true must equal EXACTLY the set of tokens that ReadinessDimensions._coarse_state can return. Adding a return to that function without flipping the flag here fails the validator, and vice versa.
rules.productionReadyNeverInferred: production_ready must have inferable=false permanently. It is a claim backed by live validation plus security review (plus external audit where required), never a shape the code deduces. The validator asserts this literally, asserts CredentialReadiness.PRODUCTION_READY never appears in _coarse_state, and asserts the honesty validator refuses state=production_ready without the evidence-backed production_ready claim.
rules.presentationIsNotCertification: Tokens in category=presentation describe the freshness/health of a rendered read (stale, partial, error, connection_testing, entitlement and credential-entry states). They never appear in the certification ladder, carry rank=null, and must never be written into a certification record or an evidence manifest.
rules.aliasUniqueness: An alias must not collide with any token id or with any other token's alias. Aliases exist so a mandated release-plan spelling can resolve onto the token the running code already serialises.
rules.releasePlanCoverage: Every token in releasePlanVocabulary must resolve to exactly one token id or alias in this file.

tokens.description: Deliberately out of scope for the current release. The capability may exist in the tree but is not shipped, not certified, and not counted by the readiness scorecard.
Turned off on purpose by an operator, a compliance hold, or a deprecation. An off-ramp state: it is not a stage on the way to live.

Progress is blocked by a third party Aether does not control — partner onboarding, regulator sign-off, or an unfulfilled provider agreement. Distinct from credential_waiting, where the credential path is open and only propagation is pending.

Previously working, now regressed: a dependency failed and the capability serves reduced or last-known data. An off-ramp state ranked below the progression so it can never satisfy an at-least-credential-waiting gate.
Runs entirely against local fixtures with no provider dependency. Honest for development; never presentable as live.
Descriptor only: decode and execution paths are not implemented. The forbidden-for-first-release marker.

Adapter code is complete and exercised by tests, but no deployment infrastructure is declared for it yet. Claimed explicitly against code-review evidence; never inferred, because passing tests do not prove a deployable surface.

Code complete and deployment infrastructure declared, but no credential has been supplied. Claimed explicitly against an infrastructure review; never inferred. Deliberately has no TypeScript binding: the presentation layer already binds the bare string 'configured' to partner_live for PaymentProviderAccount.status, so a certification-plane 'configured' must never be handed to resolveCapabilityState as a raw string.
Everything Aether controls is done; the capability is waiting on a credential to be issued, accepted, or propagated. The honest ceiling for a credentialless release.
Verified end to end against recorded/replayed provider traffic. Proves decode and mapping correctness; proves nothing about the live provider.
Verified end to end in the provider's sandbox with real credentials. Still not production: sandbox data, sandbox limits, sandbox failure modes.
Executing against the production provider with production credentials. The highest state reachable by inference from evidence.

Live-validated AND security-reviewed AND (where the provider requires it) externally audited. This is a human-backed claim, not a computed shape. It is the only certification token that is structurally unreachable by design.

guard.rule: state == CredentialReadiness.PRODUCTION_READY is rejected unless the evidence-backed production_ready claim is set, which in turn requires live_validated and security_reviewed (and externally_audited when requires_external_audit is set).

tokens.description: The tenant's plan or entitlement does not include this capability. A billing fact, not a build state.
No credentials or configuration have been supplied for this tenant yet.
Configuration is present but provider credentials are still needed from the tenant. Requires user action.
The provider rejected the supplied credentials.
A connection probe against the provider is in flight. Transient.
Data is present but older than its freshness SLA.
Some expected inputs are present, not all.
The capability read failed.
The capability is halted by an active kill switch.
